correctness.rationale: For the printed minus-sign system, the constant fiber matrix has polynomial \(\lambda^2+d\lambda+3\) and hence two strictly negative Lyapunov exponents for every \(d>0\). The invariant vertical tangent subbundle carries exactly this cocycle and the quotient is the 3D Sprott-C variational cocycle. The base divergence is \(-1\); a non-equilibrium ergodic base measure has one zero flow exponent, so at most one base exponent is positive. At the equilibria the base factor is \(\lambda^2+2\) together with \(\lambda+1\). Exact substitution gives divergence \(-1-d\), equilibria \(E_\pm=(\pm1,\pm1,0,\mp d/3,\mp1/3)\), and the stated fifth-degree factorization. The dependency-free replay checks these identities and the \(d=499/500\) signs.

originality.rationale: The inspected source itself contains an unreported split between two equations: Eq. (2) prints \(\dot s=w-ds\), whereas the equilibrium/Jacobian/divergence/characteristic-polynomial calculations correspond exactly to \(\dot s=w+ds\), and Section 5 later writes the plus-sign master/slave equations explicitly. Exact-title and equation-level searches found no erratum or paper stating this correction. Related Sprott-C papers use different equations.
residual_risks: A correction could exist under a non-obvious venue or title not indexed by the exact-title and equation-level searches.

The source does not document the exact numerical code used for Eq. (8), so the inference that its finite-time spectrum was generated from the plus-sign system is strongly supported by multiple exact identities but is not based on source-code inspection.
The no-hyperchaos theorem is restricted to compact invariant dynamics with defined Lyapunov exponents; it is not a statement about transient finite-time exponent counts on unbounded trajectories.

value.rationale: The corrected sign reverses two transverse Lyapunov exponents and changes the central classification from a claimed three-positive-exponent hyperchaotic flow to a skew product with at most one positive exponent. It also simultaneously resolves the source's equilibrium-sign, Jacobian, divergence, characteristic-polynomial, Lyapunov-sum, and synchronization-equation inconsistencies. This gives a reusable exact diagnostic for anyone studying, simulating, synchronizing, or implementing the published model.
